concepts.def: Section of DNA that codes for a specific protein and a characteristic.
One version of a gene. Most genes have two alleles, one from each parent.
Dominant allele's effect shows if one is present; recessive only shows if both are present.
The combination of alleles a person has (e.g. Bb).
Observable characteristic that results from the genotype.
Diagram for predicting offspring genotypes from parents' alleles.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Reproduction & Inheritance — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Reproduction & Inheritance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Reproduction & Inheritance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
